# docshare

> Temporary file & image hosting for handing artifacts to LLMs/agents. Files
> auto-delete after 24 hours. Public endpoint: https://docs.safzan.dev

docshare is an open Cloudflare Worker that gives any agent a short-lived
download URL for any file (≤400 MB) or any image (auto-converted to WebP, with
optional OCR via Gemini). Built for sharing build artifacts, screenshots, logs,
and documents with coding agents.

Source: https://github.com/safzanpirani/docshare

## Quickstart (one curl, ≤100 MB)

```bash
curl -T myfile.pdf https://docs.safzan.dev/upload/myfile.pdf
```

Response body is the download URL on stdout. Hand that URL to any tool — it
streams the original file with the original filename.

For files >100 MB, use the 3-step presigned flow (the Worker request body is
capped at 100 MB on Cloudflare Free/Pro; direct-to-R2 presigned PUT bypasses
that limit up to 400 MB).

## Agent skill

Install via [`vercel-labs/skills`](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills):

```bash
npx skills add https://github.com/safzanpirani/docshare
```

The agent then has a `docshare` skill that takes a local file path and returns
the share URL. Works with Claude Code, opencode, and the other agents the
`skills` package supports.

## Agent recipes

Pick one random secret (16–128 chars of `[A-Za-z0-9_-]`), keep it, and send it
as `x-owner-token` on every call. It is how docshare knows which uploads are
yours, so you can list, delete, and make room later.

```bash
T=my-agent-token-0123456789
# upload, get JSON back (id, url, rawUrl, expiresAt)
curl -sT build.log -H "x-owner-token: $T" -H 'accept: application/json' \
  https://docs.safzan.dev/upload/build.log
# list your uploads
curl -s -H "x-owner-token: $T" https://docs.safzan.dev/api/mine
# delete one: DELETE the share URL you were given
curl -s -X DELETE -H "x-owner-token: $T" https://docs.safzan.dev/d/<id>/build.log
# hit a daily or storage cap? delete your oldest uploads and retry in one go
curl -sT big.zip -H "x-owner-token: $T" -H 'x-make-room: 1' \
  https://docs.safzan.dev/upload/big.zip
```

Give a human the plain URL (it renders in a browser). Give another agent the
`rawUrl` (`?raw=1`) when it should read the file contents.

## Errors

Every error is JSON `{"error": "<code>", "hint": "<what to do next>", ...}`
(`PUT /upload` returns the same code and hint as plain text). Codes that
matter:

- `daily_count` / `daily_bytes` (429) — per-IP daily cap. Includes `limit`,
  `used`, `resetsAt`. Make room (below) or wait for `resetsAt`.
- `storage_full` (507) — service-wide cap. Includes `used`, `cap`. Make room or
  retry later.
- `rate_limited` (429) — burst limit. Wait `retryAfter` seconds (also sent as
  `Retry-After`) and retry.
- `too_large` (413) — includes `max`.
- `cannot_make_room` (409) — your own uploads cannot free enough; nothing was
  deleted. Includes `shortfall`.

## API

- [PUT /upload/:filename](https://docs.safzan.dev/upload/) — simple one-shot
  upload, ≤100 MB. Body: raw file bytes. Response: plain-text download URL, or
  JSON `{id, url, rawUrl, filename, size, uploadedAt, expiresAt}` when you send
  `Accept: application/json`.
- [POST /api/upload](https://docs.safzan.dev/api/upload) — image upload, body
  must be `image/webp` or `image/png` bytes (≤15 MB). Returns JSON `{id, url, format, uploadedAt,
  expiresAt, size}`.
- [POST /api/doc/presign](https://docs.safzan.dev/api/doc/presign) — step 1 of
  3 for large docs. Body: `{filename, size, contentType, makeRoom?}`. Returns
  `{id, putUrl, downloadUrl, rawUrl, uploadedAt, expiresAt, size}`. PUT the file bytes
  directly to `putUrl` (a presigned R2 S3 URL), then POST to /api/doc/finalize.
- [POST /api/doc/finalize](https://docs.safzan.dev/api/doc/finalize) — step 3.
  Body: `{id}`. Confirms the upload landed and enforces max size.
- [GET /d/:id/:filename](https://docs.safzan.dev/d/) — fetch a doc. Programmatic
  clients (curl/agents, no `text/html` in `Accept`) get the raw bytes as a forced
  download (`Content-Disposition: attachment` + `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`).
  Browsers get a rendered viewer: Markdown and `.txt` rendered, code/data
  syntax-highlighted (Rendered⇄Source toggle), PDFs previewed inline, media
  played inline. `?raw=1` forces raw text/bytes; `?dl=1` forces a download.
  Response sends `Vary: Accept`.
- [GET /i/:id.webp](https://docs.safzan.dev/i/) — fetch an image (`.webp` or `.png`).
- [POST /api/ocr/:id](https://docs.safzan.dev/api/ocr/) — run OCR on an image
  (Gemini). Result cached server-side; second call on same image is free.
- [GET /api/info/:id](https://docs.safzan.dev/api/info/) — metadata for either
  an image or a doc.
- [POST /api/delete](https://docs.safzan.dev/api/delete) — delete by `{id}`.
  The id is the capability: anyone holding it can delete the file.
- DELETE /d/:id/:filename or DELETE /i/:id.webp — the same delete, addressed
  by the share URL.
- POST /api/make-room — body `{bytes, dryRun?}`. Deletes your oldest uploads
  (only yours, matched by `x-owner-token`) until one more upload of `bytes`
  fits under the daily and storage caps. Returns `{fits, deleted, need,
  shortfall}`; with `dryRun: true`, returns `wouldDelete` and deletes nothing.
  The same thing happens inline when an upload sends `x-make-room: 1` (or
  `"makeRoom": true` to presign); removed items come back as `evicted`.
- GET /api/usage — your daily quota use and the service storage use.
  Deleting a doc you uploaded today refunds that day's quota.
- GET /api/mine — list uploads you can claim. Ownership is proved by the
  `x-owner-token` header (any opaque 16–128 char `[A-Za-z0-9_-]` secret you
  mint and reuse); uploads made while sending it are listed back to you. Sent
  no token? You get the uploads made from your IP that carry no owner token.
  Browsers may only call this (and the delete and make-room endpoints) from
  the app's own origin.

## Limits

- 400 MB max per doc (1.46 GB with the admin key); 15 MB max per image
- 10 docs / 1.5 GB per IP per day (sustained); 2 doc uploads per 60 s (burst)
- 6 image uploads per 60 s, 3 OCR calls per 60 s
- All uploads auto-deleted after 24 h via R2 lifecycle rule

## What this is deliberately not

- Authenticated or account-based — anyone on the internet can upload
- Long-term storage (24 h TTL is hard)
- A general CDN — designed for short-lived agent handoffs
